title: Govt notifies E100 as auto fuel for flex-fuel vehicles
syllabus: GS3 › Infrastructure: energy; Environment (pollution); Agriculture-linked industry
context: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways amended the Central Motor Vehicle Rules to allow flex-fuel vehicles to run on up to E100 (nearly pure ethanol). Ordinary petrol or E20 vehicles cannot use E100.
ideas: Ethanol reduces dependence on imported crude oil.
GS3 · Energy security
Higher ethanol blends such as E100 cut India's dependence on imported crude.
Lower lifecycle emissions are possible, but they depend on the crop and the production process.
GS3 · Environment (balanced view)
Ethanol's climate benefit depends on the crop and process used, so lifecycle emissions must be counted.
keywords: Crops for ethanol compete with crops for food and water
Biofuel policy must manage the food-vs-fuel trade-off over land and water.
Vehicle built to run on different petrol-ethanol blends
Flex-fuel vehicles, now allowed to run on E100, offer a parallel route to cleaner transport alongside EVs.
Emissions across production, transport and use
Judged by lifecycle emissions, not tailpipe alone, biofuels are not automatically green.
Ethanol blending reduces import dependence and the oil import bill.
pyqs: Higher ethanol blends reduce dependence on imported crude.
Flex-fuel vehicles as a parallel route to cleaner transport alongside EVs.
links: Related Explained: Centre clears way for flex-fuel up to E100
summary: Flex-fuel vehicles may now run on E100, nearly pure ethanol; ordinary petrol and E20 vehicles cannot.
evolution: Ongoing debate over the use of E20 fuel (as the report notes).
E100 notified, but only for vehicles built as flex-fuel.

title: Punjab farm fires: why most stubble-burning incidents are in two districts
syllabus: GS3 › Environmental pollution; Cropping patterns; Agricultural technology · GS4 › Ethical dilemmas: private gain vs public good
context: Punjab has recorded 684 farm fires this season, 457 of them (69%) in Tarn Taran and Amritsar. Early harvesting of short-duration paddy in the Majha region lets farmers fit in a third crop of peas or potatoes before wheat, which leaves little time to clear fields without burning.
ideas: The real cause is the crop calendar, not just a lack of machines.
GS3 · Stubble burning
Stubble burning in Majha is driven by the crop calendar, not merely a lack of machines.
Fires are falling year on year; support and awareness matter as much as penalties.
GS3 policy · GS4 persuasion
Falling farm fires show that support and awareness work alongside penalties.
Leaving the paddy-wheat cycle is the long-term fix (see Manauli's sweet-corn shift).
GS3 · Crop diversification
Moving out of the paddy-wheat cycle, as Manauli did, is the long-term fix for stubble burning.
keywords: Farmers stuck in one crop cycle by MSP and habit
A paddy-wheat lock-in leaves farmers little choice but to burn straw before the next crop.
A private act that imposes costs on others
Stubble burning is a negative externality: a private saving that imposes health costs on millions.
Handling straw in the field / removing it for use elsewhere
In-situ and ex-situ residue management offer alternatives to burning.
Moving to a wider mix of crops
Crop diversification is the durable answer to stubble burning and groundwater stress.
data: Farm fires by this point in the season, 2024 → 2025 → 2026
Punjab's farm fires fell from 1,857 (2024) to 743 (2025) to 684 (2026) by the same point in the season.
Despite 1.25 lakh residue-management machines, Punjab still sees farm fires.
examples: About 70% of 2,000 acres moved from paddy to sweet corn and vegetables; farmers formed an FPO
Manauli in Haryana moved about 70% of its land from paddy to sweet corn and vegetables and formed an FPO.
pyqs: Majha's third crop and Manauli's shift to sweet corn show diversification in practice.
Why farmers choose high-value crops: Manauli's returns and market links.
Farm fires and clean air: 684 fires so far against 743 last year and 1,857 in 2024.
summary: Most of Punjab's farm fires this season are in Tarn Taran and Amritsar, where a third crop leaves farmers too little time to clear fields without burning.
evolution: 1,857 fires by this point in the season.
684 fires so far, but an early spike in Majha.

title: Delhi plans a bottle-return scheme, taking a cue from Uttarakhand and Goa
syllabus: GS3 › Solid waste management; Conservation · GS4 › Environmental ethics in public administration
context: Delhi is considering a Deposit Refund Scheme (DRS) in which consumers pay an extra Re 1 or Rs 2 for a plastic bottle and get it back on return, possibly using QR codes and starting with tourist spots.
ideas: A small refundable deposit changes behaviour more than appeals alone.
GS3 · Waste management
A small refundable deposit changes behaviour more than appeals alone.
It moves people from 'use and throw' to 'use, return and recover': a circular economy.
GS3 environment · Essay
Deposit schemes move citizens from 'use and throw' to 'use, return and recover'.
Environmental ethics in public administration: the state designs incentives so that the right choice becomes the easy one.
GS4 · Environmental ethics
In a deposit scheme the state designs incentives so the environmentally right choice becomes the easy one.
keywords: Changing behaviour through incentives, not orders
A refundable deposit is a nudge: behaviour change without coercion.
Producers made responsible for their products' waste
Extended Producer Responsibility makes producers accountable for their plastic waste.
Reusing and recycling materials to cut waste
A circular economy keeps materials in use and cuts waste.
Refundable deposit on containers to encourage return
Deposit refund schemes, as in Uttarakhand and Goa, raise container returns.
data: Bottle return rate in Uttarakhand after its deposit scheme
Uttarakhand's deposit scheme raised bottle returns from about 20% to nearly 90%.
Delhi govt report, via IE p. 11
Delhi generates about 1,500 tonnes of plastic waste a day.
examples: Won a Digital India Award and was expanded across Uttarakhand
Uttarakhand's Kedarnath deposit refund pilot (2022) won a Digital India Award and was scaled statewide.
pyqs: Directly usable: Delhi's 1,500 tonnes of plastic waste a day, 19% unprocessed, and the deposit-refund fix.
Deposit-refund schemes as a collection model: Uttarakhand's returns rose from about 20% to nearly 90%.
Use the bottle-return scheme as an environmental issue seen through environmental ethics.
summary: Delhi plans a refundable deposit on plastic bottles, copying schemes that already work in Uttarakhand and Goa.
evolution: Single-use plastic items banned across India.
Uttarakhand's pilot at Kedarnath; returns rose from about 20-22% to nearly 90%.
Goa runs a Rs 5 deposit; Delhi plans its own scheme.
